decisions.reason: As a very recent launch with its own web presence and a strong fit with the firm's customizable drainage platform, its results are likely still being judged as promising enough to keep under normal organizational slack.

A floor-level shower drainage system is central to the firm's stated strategic direction toward integrated, accessible bathroom solutions, so management would likely retain it unless early results were clearly below aspiration.
Its design-oriented positioning matches the firm's customer base and differentiation logic, and a one-year-old product would usually be given more time before being dropped.
The integrated-slope shower element supports installation ease and renovation use cases, so despite limited market evidence management would likely continue it while learning about demand.
The product addresses a specific, credible drainage problem and was prominently launched, which suggests enough initial commitment and problem-solution clarity to keep it on the market.

Because an air-admittance valve is somewhat more peripheral to the firm's core premium shower-drainage focus and was only mentioned briefly, it faces the highest review risk, but it is still likely to be kept for now given its recent launch and portfolio complementarity.
